title: Operational limits of reference renewal for retained quantum-service results: reproducibility artifact
description:
Public reproducibility package for the author preprint Operational limits of reference renewal for retained quantum-service results, prepared for Quantum Information Processing, collection Quantum Software Engineering. This is a bounded physical implementation and operational-limits study, not an accepted article.

Twelve context transitions retained six physical results each. Ten completed renewal, eight met the prespecified endpoint and five succeeded using retained results alone. The exact one-sided p=0.0546875 does not establish H1-B. A retrospective binding-plus-oracle rule accepts all 60 usable-window physical results and separately the 12 results in C05/C09. The evidence does not demonstrate incremental numerical-correctness utility of reference renewal over direct oracle checking.

The unchanged v5.1 artifact reconstructs matrices, scores, ranks, decisions, endpoints and statistics from 575 count-bearing units and 429 scores in eleven complete references. It includes incomplete transitions, a separate post-campaign KC-B4 correction and descriptive context comparisons. Both ordinary and isolated Python invocation are supported in the tested environment. The public package includes paper PDFs, editable sources, code, deidentified inputs, manifests and verification instructions. The public wrapper only adds citation, licensing and archival information; no new physical experiment or scientific analysis is introduced.

Numerical reproduction is conditional on recorded operational states and clocks. It does not revalidate private HMAC authentication, provider authenticity, the full acquisition state machine or independent pre-acquisition temporal precedence.
